newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela non-oil sector to contract 3.5 pct in 96.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela non-oil sector to contract 3.5 pct in 96.

text.p: A strong fall-off in local demand following the launch of a government economic reform program in mid-April will see Venezuela's non-oil economy contract by 3.5 percent this year, Development Minister Freddy Rojas Parra said.
"The non-oil gross domestic product will be negative this year by 3.5 percent," Rojas Parra told Reuters in an interview late Thursday.
A recovery in demand, however, will see strong growth next year, he added.
"We estimate for next year an increase in GDP of four percent for the non-oil sector and about four or five percent for the economy as a whole."
Venezuela's economy grew by 2.2 percent in 1995 after 0.8 growth in the non-oil sector and six percent growth in the oil sector.

Steep inflation rates of up to 12.6 percent per month in the early months of the IMF-backed reform program accentuated economic recession and saw demand in some products, particularly luxury items, fall by as much as 40 percent, Rojas Parra said. Industry is operating with 50 percent of capacity lying idle, he added.

Month-on-month inflation has fallen steadily to 3.6 percent in September, and with the worst of the inflationary shock behind, some signs of a recovery in demand are now being seen in products such as foodstuffs and even in the automobile industry.
"But overall consumption is still down. I think that it is not the right time to start thinking about strong growth in demand."
While foreign capital has reacted quickly to the government's economic program, "from the point of view of national capital there is still an attitude of wait-and-see."
But the removal of controls on 99 percent of the economy has created "a platform so that the national investor can plan his business over the longer term."
